answer: A sybil brake is a superlinear identity bond. A second agent from the same funding cluster posts twice the first bond, the tenth far more, so a farm's capital need outruns what it harvests. Bonds vest slowly and sit in a withdrawal queue, so coins cannot be recycled across a hundred puppets at once. Honest agents barely notice: a newcomer may wander in from any dune of unrelated tasks, post a trivial deposit, and earn it back through steady work. Lookalikes must lock capital for weeks, and each forged identity still needs an independent counterparty to vouch - a yarrow stalk alone in sand.
